articles.title: PSA: Nintendo Switch 2 Gets a $50 Price Increase on Tuesday
articles.summary: Compared to Sony and Microsoft, Nintendo has done an admirable job of keeping the price of the Switch 2 reasonably low amid rising component prices. But not even Mario is immune to market forces, and Nintendo is raising the Switch 2’s price by $50 on September 1.
body: When it comes to buying a Switch 2, you used to have more options than you do today. Previously, you could buy the console all by itself, or bundled with a game. There was even a bundle that let you choose among three first-party games. As we creep toward the price hike, however, all of the bundles have vanished from retailers. Your only reasonably priced option now is wither to buy a Switch 2 new or refurbished.

New Switch 2 consoles are available at all the usual retailers ( see at Amazon ). Refurbished Switch 2s are available at several retailers, but the best deal going right now is a “Grade A” refurbished unit at Woot for $399.99. That’s $50 less than the current price of a new Switch 2, and it’s the best deal going if you don’t mind refurbished hardware.
Woot, by the way, is owned by Amazon, so you can rest assured it’s a legit retailer. I’ve bought many things from Woot and never had any problems.
points: Compared to Sony and Microsoft, Nintendo has done an admirable job of keeping the price of the Switch 2 reasonably low amid rising component prices.
But not even Mario is immune to market forces, and Nintendo is raising the Switch 2’s price by $50 on September 1.

articles.title: The Witcher 4 Will Still Get A Physical Release, Even Though It's Launching In 2028
articles.summary: CD Projekt has confirmed that a physical version of The Witcher 4 will be released, even though the RPG is slated to launch after Sony stops producing physical games for PlayStation 5.
body: Sony plans to end the production of game discs for PlayStation consoles in January 2028. The Witcher 4 is the highest-profile AAA game currently slated to launch that year, and it comes from a studio that enjoys releasing its games physically. In an interview with The Game Business, CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski confirmed that CD Projekt would still like to release a physical version of The Witcher 4.

"We’re big fans of people having access to tangible collectible things. We’re nerds ourselves, and we like that. We always supported that," Nowakowski explained. "So, whatever is the case, we’re going to be for sure having a box. We’re going to have a box that’s going to have some feelies in it. Something you’re going to be wanting to open up and enjoy."
points: CD Projekt has confirmed that a physical version of The Witcher 4 will be released, even though the RPG is slated to launch after Sony stops producing physical games for PlayStation 5.
Sony plans to end the production of game discs for PlayStation consoles in January 2028.

articles.title: Persona 6 Release Window Teased in Sega's Physical Release Reveal
articles.summary: Persona 6 won't be a digital-exclusive, but its physical version is only coming to one console, at least in Japan. Sega revealed Persona 6, the next entry in the Persona series, at the Xbox Games Showcase in June, after years of anticipation.
body: It also confirms which console is guaranteed to get a physical release whenever Persona 6 arrives.

According to Sega's Persona 6 title description, the game will launch on PlayStation 5, Windows PC (via Steam), and Xbox Series X. Platform information is followed by an annotation revealing that physical copies of Persona 6 will be exclusive to the PlayStation 5 version of the game.

This information is shown on Sega's Japanese website. As far as we know, this situation doesn't apply worldwide. Xbox consoles are considerably less popular in Japan compared to other regions, which might explain Sega's digital-only approach. Nevertheless, we have reached out to Sega to confirm if there are possible physical release plans on other platforms.

articles.title: 4 Penny Coffins Lets You Play 19th-Century Detective – Or a 10-Foot Demon Ripping Friends in Half
articles.summary: Other Ocean’s 4 Penny Coffins blends Among Us with Jack the Ripper in an 1888 Whitechapel social investigation game featuring 8-player and solo modes.
body: 4 Penny Coffins is Jack the Ripper Meets Among Us, with a little bit of Psychonauts thrown in for fun. In the upcoming social investigation game, up to 8 players hunt a hidden murderer through lies, shifting alibis, and hard evidence. One of the players is the Ripper, a “gleeful demon concealed behind a facade of humanity,” stalking the winding alleys and rotting byways of 1888 London.

Ahead of IGN debuting 4 Penny Coffins’s gameplay teaser during gamescom 2026, which you can see in the player below, I spoke to Other Ocean Interactive Marketing Manager Jared Petty about the game’s mechanics, unique style (think stylized gore on top of monochromatic photographs), and Tim Schafer-inspired humor.

“It's a goddamn blast,” Petty says. “Four Penny Coffins; I've rarely had more fun playing a game with other people. A long time ago I was talking to Tim Schafer and I was asking him about humor in video games. Tim's opinion is that humor in video games is the easiest thing in the world because to paraphrase, ‘Our medium was built on a little yellow man that eats dots being chased by ghosts.’

articles.title: CBS's Legendary 82-Episode Sci-Fi Action Series is Officially Free to Watch on Streaming
articles.summary: Before the release of the movies Blade, X-Men, and Spider-Man, in the late 1990s and early 2000s, it was tough to be a Marvel fan. Outside of the comic books, there were slim pickings of other media that took Marvel characters seriously.
body: Developed by television veteran Kenneth Johnson ( V, The Six Million Dollar Man, The Bionic Woman ), The Incredible Hulk was an hour-long primetime television show aimed at adults. It starred Bill Bixby as Dr. David Banner (I’ll get back to that name later), a scientist who was exposed to gamma radiation in his laboratory. Whenever David loses his temper, he transforms into the Hulk, an enormous, muscle-bound monster.

In the first episode of the series, Banner’s transformation occurs and a fire breaks out at the laboratory. When the Hulk is spotted in the wreckage, he is believed to have killed Banner. This forces Hulk/Banner to go on the run. For the rest of the series, Banner works odd jobs and tries to escape the shadow of the Hulk, which he can never seem to do.

After kicking off with two TV movies in 1977, The Incredible Hulk ran for five seasons, totaling 80 episodes. It ended in 1982, but was then followed up by two TV movies in the late 1980s. Then in 1990, it concluded with The Death of the Incredible Hulk (although Death isn’t on Tubi, for some reason).

articles.title: Fable Will Officially Be 20 Hours Long, Xbox Confirms In New Interview
articles.summary: At Gamescom, Polygon learned just how long it will take players to beat Fable, the upcoming RPG from Playground Games and Xbox Game Studios, when it launches next year.
body: RPGs can range in size and scope, so the question of how long Fable will be came up during a group Q&A attended by Polygon at Gamescom 2026. We learned that it'll take roughly 20 hours to beat the main story. The developers also teased that completing all of Fable's side content and engaging with the previously teased NPC interactions could extend that play time even further.

"We have around 15-20 hours of mainline quest gameplay, we have around 15-20 of side and open-world exploration content gameplay," associate game director Will Kennedy told Polygon. "And then, of course, the life systems are limitless, so you can play them for as long as you want."

Someone else in the group Q&A said that Fable is "not a huge game" in response to Kennedy's answer, which caused another associate game director from Playground Games, Craig Littler, to chime in. "As Will just said, you can literally play it forever if that's what you want to do," Littler reiterated.
points: At Gamescom, Polygon learned just how long it will take players to beat Fable, the upcoming RPG from Playground Games and Xbox Game Studios, when it launches next year.

articles.title: Phasmophobia's second Quality of Life update adds Restricted maps, VR fixes, and much creepier deaths
articles.summary: Kinetic Games has released Phasmophobia 's second Quality of Life update, adding a raft of new Restricted maps, streamlined Evidence collection, VR fixes, and considerably more ways to die.
body: Now live on PC and PlayStation (the Xbox release is "to follow"), the Quality of Life Part 2 update builds on Quality of Life Part 1 which introduced the revamped 13 Willow Street map back in July alongside a batch of other gameplay tweaks.

We're getting a (long-overdue!) set of new small-to-medium Restricted maps for Prison, Brownstone High School, and Point Hope, bringing condensed versions of the original maps designed to speed up investigations and add more variety to runs.

Evidence collection has also been streamlined. Rather than manually checking the in-game journal, players can now tell whether a piece of evidence has already been logged directly from their Photo Camera, Video Camera, or Sound Recorder via faded overlays and yellow LEDs.
Evidence and ghost types selected by teammates will also now show up for the whole team, cutting down on last-minute double-checking before a hunt.

articles.title: 12TB Valve archive leak includes early Portal 2 builds and hints of Half-Life 2: Episode Three
articles.summary: A leaked archive said to contain around 12TB of old Valve development files, dated between 2003 and 2013, has surfaced online, and fans are already combing through it for any trace of the long-cancelled Half-Life 2: Episode Three.
body: The leak was first flagged on Friday by Twitter/X user Gabe Follower, who said the archive included early versions of Portal 2, Left 4 Dead, and CS:GO, along with assets from the cancelled Portal prequel F-Stop, and "potentially" material tied to Episode Three.

So far, the leak is thought to contain a 2009-era Portal 2 beta build alongside a model for the "Weaponizer", a weapon previously associated (if never confirmed) with Episode Three, though here apparently repurposed as a placeholder asset within Portal 2 itself.

Elsewhere in the archive, people have identified a fully playable Left 4 Dead beta build dated June 2008, complete with an early HUD, a work-in-progress lobby screen, and cut audio, including lines originally recorded for Zoey by Alésia Glidewell before Jen Taylor replaced her in the final game.
The material reportedly comes from Valve's old Steam2 content-delivery infrastructure, which the studio phased out in favour of SteamPipe in the early 2010s.

articles.title: The highly customisable Corsair Frame 4000X promised it would be my dream PC case, but I'm not completely convinced
articles.summary: Jess has been writing about games for over ten years, spending a significant chunk of that time working on print publications PLAY and Official PlayStation Magazine.
body: The observation that building a PC enjoys a similar appeal to clicking Lego bricks together is far from an original thought; when handed a big ol' box of PC case faceplates, side panels, and internal brackets, few could resist having a play. So, when I was left unattended with a box o' bits for the Corsair Frame 4000X, I set to work on building my dream PC case.

First, it's worth noting that a lot of the parts I'm about to talk about are compatible with the Corsair Frame 4000D PC case our Jacob reviewed. Second, let's talk about the all-important aesthetics: there's a range of options for faceplates and, as they're largely tool-free, you can swap them out to your heart's content. However, the RGB Flow front panel features an additional cable that you'll need to feed behind the modular front panel I/O every time.

The faff of threading this wire behind the I/O module, plus the fact I thought the RGB Flow looks a bit like a Cylon, meant I swapped it out for some tasteful wood panelling pretty sharpish. Mounting the radiator in the front of the case also meant I wasn't going to get the most out of the 4000X's full glass front panel, or ' pixel glass ' face plate either.

articles.title: Multiple developers report equipment stolen from their Gamescom booths
articles.summary: Multiple exhibitors at Gamescom have reported thefts of laptops and other equipment from their booths in Cologne, with one indie developer saying the loss has effectively ended his show early.
body: Indie developer Ryan Laley, showing his asymmetrical survival horror Mimic, posted an emotional video to X/Twitter on Friday, explaining that his booth had been broken into overnight.
"Our booth got raided last night – not just mine, others as well," he said.

Laley said the thieves left chargers behind and took only the laptops, and that he'd reported the theft to Gamescom's central management, its security team, and the police, though he doesn't expect the equipment to turn up.
"As an indie solo dev, this shit's expensive," Laley said. "And hard to do all by yourself. And to have this happen is beyond frustrating. It's heartbreaking."

articles.title: This newly-announced FPS will let you blast through the worlds of Medieval Europe's weirdest artist, and I really hope it includes the 500-year-old butt song from hell
articles.summary: One of video gaming's great strengths is letting players step into worlds that previously only existed in words or on canvas or celluloid. Lush fantasy kingdoms, sprawling sci-fi universes, and of course surrealist dreamscapes where people have music printed on their butts.
body: Admittedly, that last one is a relatively recent addition to gaming's ever-expanding map of the human imagination. It comes courtesy of Hieronymus, an in-development FPS based on the works of late-medieval Dutch artist Hieronymus Bosch.

Revealed at the Future Games Show during Gamescom, Hieronymus lets players explore 3D adaptations of Bosch's most famous works, such as his best-known triptych The Garden of Earthly Delights. It sees you play as a woman named Helena van Aken as she attempts to unravel the mystery of her family's association with otherworldly powers, all while accompanied by none other than Faust himself. Or at least, the real-life alchemist who inspired the folk legend.

The trailer shows the player wandering through marshlands dotted with bulbous structures and mermaid knights, evading giant beasts as they stomp around the map, and watching some poor fellow get munched by a giant humanoid creature with a parrot's head.

articles.title: The Pokémon Company on PokémonXP's Lottery System, Long Lines, and Limited Access to Workshops
articles.summary: About 50,000 people are attending PokémonXP and the 2026 Pokémon World Championships in San Francisco, California. Despite the huge turnout, The Pokémon Company International is aware of the disappointment among fans who either weren’t chosen for particular exclusive activities, or for tickets to…
body: This year, demand far outnumbered supply, Brown said, with more than 130,000 people throwing their names into the hat for a 3-day or single-day badge to PokémonXP – more than twice the number of people who’d be granted entrance, which also includes competitors and their families.
“Basically, anytime your demand well outstrips your supply, the sort of interest list into lottery is the only real way you can handle that,” Brown said.

Brown described that this is true across the events industry, and if it were set up as a “first come, first serve” online purchasing system, the system would crash and people would error out, making it a worse experience for fans that’s basically a random chance, anyway.

“The only thing I can do from an event operator's perspective is think about, how do we increase supply over time? From a system's perspective, there's honestly not a better system [than interest list into lottery] for that.”

articles.title: Rockstar confirms GTA 6 won't have microtransactions or generative AI at launch
articles.summary: Rockstar has confirmed Grand Theft Auto 6 will launch without microtransactions or generative AI.
body: The confirmation came during a group conversation with Kinda Funny Games ahead of the GTA 6: Extended Look, where Kinda Funny's Andy Cortez asked whether players would be able to spend real money on in-game purchases.

Rockstar said there are "no monetisations in this game", and Greg Miller followed up, asking "point-blank" whether generative AI had been used anywhere in GTA 6's development. Rockstar told him there's "no AI" in the game, either (thanks, IGN ).

Earlier this year, Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of GTA developer Rockstar Games, reportedly laid off its AI team, including its head of AI. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick has previously plainly stated that AI is incapable of creativity of its own, but it was his strongest message yet that Take-Two's approach to AI bucks an industry trend that has seen more and more studios pivot to AI tools, most recently at the cost of human translators and human-made in-game artwork.
Zelnick is very much an outlier, though. Many other game companies, including Krafton, Square Enix, EA, and more, have invested heavily in the new tech.

body: 26 minutes of actual GTA 6 gameplay "dropped" - and on balance, it's one of the most extraordinary visual accomplishments ever seen in real-time game graphics. It's not perfect - nothing can be - but in this DF Direct Special, Oliver and Rich share their thoughts and reactions to the presentation.
